context_requirements: Functional OPRM1/OPRK1/OPRD1 G-protein signalling; canonical MOR/KOR/DOR coupling is largely cAMP-inhibitory and post-translational, so it does not engage the transcriptional programme measured here
Neuronal or neuroendocrine lineage for the neuroprotective/STAT3 and Nrf2/HO-1 effects reported in vivo; none of the nine lines are neuronal
In vivo ischaemia/reperfusion or inflammatory context for the reported anti-apoptotic and antioxidant effects; absent in a 6-24 h monolayer drug exposure
falsifiers: Reproducible, dose-dependent changes in the 978 landmark genes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines after 10 micromolar opioid agonist
Enrichment of a cAMP/CREB or MAPK/ERK transcriptional signature (e.g. FOS, JUN, EGR1, DUSP1/4/6, NR4A-family) that is blocked by naloxone or by OPRM1/OPRK1 knockdown
Induction of apoptosis or oxidative-stress landmark genes (e.g. PMAIP1, BAX, HMOX1, TXNRD1, GADD45A) in a receptor-dependent manner

evidence.supports: KOR agonist BRL52537 neuroprotection in rat cerebral I/R is attributed to up-regulation of phosphorylated STAT3 and reduced caspase-3, an in vivo neuronal context not represented by these cell lines

MOR agonist promotes circulating tumour cell formation in bladder cancer via MOR/AKT/Slug, indicating receptor-dependent transcriptional effects in a urological tumour context rather than a broad landmark-gene response
KOR agonist U50488H reduces myocardial apoptosis and infarct size after I/R in rats, an in vivo cardioprotective effect
KOR agonist U50488H protects against myocardial injury in heart failure rats via Nrf2/HO-1 and Ca2+-SERCA2a regulation
KOR agonist U50488H attenuates postoperative cognitive dysfunction in rats through PI3K/AKT/Nrf2/HO-1, again an in vivo neuroprotective mechanism
